purpose: Convert the B03 safety contract into a testable dry-run protocol: a request/response schema for Codex -> MCP -> local CLI worker prompt+command composition, reusing EXISTING dry-run code (cli_adapter_dryrun.build_argv_template/validate_command, core.check_runner_topic_allowlist) as the composition/validation engine. No new process-launch or subprocess code is added by this task; allowed_writes contains no src/ path.

reused_implementation.note: This protocol adds zero new execution code; it is a schema+test artifact layered on already-existing, already-tested dry-run primitives.

task_id.description: must be a task known to taskctl; checked read-only via `taskctl.py show <task_id>`

action.description: taskctl action this composed request is for; consumed by core.check_runner_topic_allowlist

mode.note: a 'live' value is rejected with decision=launch_blocked_disabled; never silently promoted

would_run_argv.description: from build_argv_template; [] for deepseek_manual (no local process)

command_allowlist_check.description: from validate_command(would_run_argv); skipped/not_applicable_manual_handoff for deepseek_manual since no local argv exists

runner_topic_check.description: from core.check_runner_topic_allowlist(runner, topic, action); reason='unknown_runner_topic_pair' when the pair is not statically allowlisted

task_id_binding_check.description: read-only `taskctl.py show <task_id>` lookup; found=false for an unknown task_id; never mutates task status

allowed_writes_check.description: cross-reference against the claimed card's allowed_writes (from `taskctl.py contract <task_id>`); real enforcement remains taskctl.py cmd_stage/cmd_guard_staged, this field only documents that binding for the composed prompt

review_return_envelope.description: identical shape to B03 review_packet_fields; produced when the worker calls `taskctl.py review <task_id> --runner <runner>` (never `done`)

prompt_composition_policy.formula: composed_prompt = `taskctl.py contract <task_id>` stdout (compact JSON) + "\n---read_first---\n" + newline-joined read_first path STRINGS (paths only, not file content -- the worker reads read_first itself; matches B03 section 7.2)
prompt_composition_policy.over_budget_policy: truncate_and_flag: composed_prompt[:budget-len(marker)] + marker, prompt_truncated=true; decision is NOT blocked by truncation alone (no silent loss -- prompt_truncated is always surfaced in the response)

measured_example_this_task.measured_via: python3 AITools/taskctl.py contract CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_AGENT_LAUNCHER_DRYRUN_PROTOCOL_B04_V1 (real command, no execution of any launch)

dry_run_examples.note: All three would_run_argv / command_allowlist_check / runner_topic_check values below are REAL measured output of cli_adapter_dryrun.build_argv_template/validate_command and core.check_runner_topic_allowlist -- not hand-written prose. No process was started to produce them.

example_codex_cli_blocked_precondition.finding: REAL gap discovered while building this protocol: core.RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST has no 'task_mcp' topic entry and no pattern for per-wave runner names like 'claude_task_mcp_launcher_dryrun_b04' (it only lists stable topic-continuous runners: claude_coding/coding, claude_stem/stem, deepseek_finance/finance, etc, plus a codex wildcard). A composed request using THIS task's own (runner, topic) would be blocked at the runner_topic_check precondition if it ever went through core.run_taskctl(). This is command-allowlist-valid but precondition-blocked -- proposed as follow-up (see next_wave).

response.handoff_note: no local process is ever composed for deepseek_manual; orchestrator renders (prompt + task card + cwd + runner/topic) for a human to paste into the externally hosted session, per B03 section 7.3

neural_bridge_note.doctrine: neural-control-first: adapter/runner/topic SELECTION for a real launch must be a learned routing + abstain decision, never a regex/keyword cue router
neural_bridge_note.this_protocol_is: a static human-authored request/response schema + reuse of an already-static safety allowlist (core.check_runner_topic_allowlist); it composes and validates, it does not route/select intelligently

rollback.rollback_action: git revert this eval JSON + next_wave JSON + test script; no runtime/registry/subprocess code exists to unwind
